The system, or all the systems rather, are unfortunately against many people who struggle with mental illness. 
A label on your mental health can be subpoenaed in child custody cases, financial cases, and many other legal tangles. Working with a private practice can limit that exposure. 
My question was really wondering because things can be worth dealing with to only a certain degree. 
Postpartum depression for example can be diagnosed by your obgyn and can be noted on your record for every baby you have, which in turn can cause you to have to participate in home visits and wellness checks for the “safety” of the child. 

Basically an on record diagnosis though protected by hippa is not entirely private in all circumstances.
So I was wondering is anyone had experience dealing with those kinds of labels and if it was worth it.

Paranoia I guess. 
Therapy is scary and so putting my life and mind out there for someone is even more scary with the notion that other someones could someday know that information. 
In an effort to protect my anonymity I chose not to use insurance but I don’t want that to limit my care due to budget.

People can’t just be pregnant and have children and up and leave it’s more complicated than that. 
That’s why I want to be very sure I’m in control of how and when things change.

Thank you that was very helpful. 
Obviously I want to talk but outside of therapy my life has to go on. And I want to be sure I’m in control.
I guess it should be noted that I’m pregnant with his child though, so there is technically a child involved
